dst: Informatics and Computer Science · 7th grade · class 012
By the end of the lesson, the student will be able to:
•  explain the parts of an email address and create an account;
•  compose, format, and send a message with an attachment and hyperlink;
•  organize mail with labels and filters;
•  recognize spam and phishing and protect personal data;
•  apply the rules of polite written communication.
email address · subject · attachment · label · filter · spam · phishing
At the end: 6 questions, one message analysis, and a group check.
How many emails do you send weekly? What is easier for you — a message or an email? Why?

dst: Informatics and Computer Science · 7th grade · class 012
A category you add to a message: Informatics, Homework, Projects. One message can have multiple labels.
Rule: if the sender or subject meets the condition → add a label, move or archive the message.
•  labels do not delete messages — they only group them;
•  the filter works automatically, even when you are not at the computer;
•  good order in the mail saves time and prevents you from missing an assignment.

Unwanted, mass messages: advertisements, fake winnings, scams.
•  contains a suspicious link or attachment.

1. Do not open the message.

3. Report as spam.

5. If you opened it — report to an adult.

dst: Phishing — when a message "fishes" for data
Informatics and Computer Science · 7th grade · class 012
Phishing is an attempt to obtain a password, card details, or money through a fake message.
The address does not belong to the school or institution, even if the name looks familiar.
The domain in the link is not official: e.g., skola-nalog.brzalogin.xyz.
Password, card number, OTP code — should never be sent via email.
Never enter a password through a link in a message. Open the site directly.
What sign is the most reliable signal that the message is fake?
